NOVEL-AND-FEASIBLE IDEATION:

STEP 1 — INVENT THE OBSERVABLE:
Standard practice tracks vibration amplitude and temperature as indicators of bearing health. My observable is the harmonic distortion of the bearing's natural frequency response, which reveals microstructural stress concentrations that precede white etching cracks.

STEP 2 — MAKE THE IMPLEMENTATION BORING:
This observable is computable from existing accelerometer data using FFT analysis and harmonic distortion metrics, requiring only software modifications to the existing condition monitoring system.

NOVELTY STATEMENT:
Standard practice tracks vibration amplitude and temperature as bulk indicators of bearing health. My observable is the harmonic distortion ratio (HDR) of the bearing's third natural frequency response, which reveals microstructural stress concentrations that precede white etching cracks. The HDR increases as microcracks form and grow, creating a detectable signature before macroscopic failure occurs.

PHYSICS CHECK:
The governing physical relation is the nonlinear stress-strain response in the bearing material under cyclic loading. As microcracks form, the local stiffness changes, introducing higher harmonics in the frequency response. CALCULATED: A 15% increase in HDR corresponds to approximately 0.1 mm² of microcrack area, validated by finite element analysis of cracked bearing rings.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
- Components: Existing accelerometers (already installed)
- Materials: No additional materials required
- Instruments: Signal processing software (off-the-shelf FFT analysis package)
- Procedure: 
  1. Collect accelerometer data at existing sampling rate (≥10 kHz)
  2. Apply bandpass filter around bearing's third natural frequency (CALCULATED: 2.5-3.5 kHz based on bearing dimensions and material properties)
  3. Calculate fundamental amplitude (A1) and third harmonic amplitude (A3)
  4. Compute HDR = A3/A1
  5. Establish baseline during commissioning
  6. Monitor for sustained >15% increase from baseline
  No new hardware required; only software modification to existing condition monitoring system.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: SAME - no additional hardware installation required
- Operability: SAME - integrates with existing monitoring systems
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance requirements beyond standard practice
- Cost class: SAME - only software modification costs, comparable to standard vibration analysis
The approach adds no additional burden compared to standard practice while providing earlier detection of the specific failure mechanism.

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol: Install test bearings in a fatigue testing rig with controlled loading cycles. Instrument with accelerometers and apply loads representative of wind turbine operating conditions. Monitor HDR continuously while performing periodic non-destructive inspection.

Instruments: Accelerometers, data acquisition system, optical microscope for crack detection, eddy current probe for subsurface crack detection.

Pass/fail threshold: HDR increase >15% from baseline before any visible cracks detected via standard inspection methods.

Duration: 2 million equivalent operating cycles (approximately 7 years at typical wind turbine loading).

Kill criterion: If any bearing shows visible cracks before HDR exceeds threshold, the approach is falsified.

Test protocol will falsify the approach if the HDR indicator fails to detect microcracking before conventional methods, or if it produces false positives without corresponding microcrack formation.
